title: Departments With Above-Average Headcount
description:
Considering only departments that have at least one employee, report the `name` of every department whose headcount is strictly above the average headcount across those departments.

Name the column `name`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT d.name
FROM departments d
WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM employees e WHERE e.dept_id = d.id) >
      (SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id));
hint: The first subquery is correlated (one department's own headcount); the second is not (the average headcount across all staffed departments) — mixing a correlated and a non-correlated subquery in the same WHERE clause is fine.
outputExplanation: Engineering (4 employees) and Sales (3) both have above-average headcount. HR (1 employee) falls below the average of about 2.67.
schemaSql:
CREATE TABLE departments (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  location TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE employees (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  title TEXT,
  salary INTEGER,
  dept_id INTEGER,
  manager_id INTEGER,
  hire_date TEXT
);

Employees with NULL department and NULL salary
Single employee, single department
tests.seedSql:

INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Solo','Engineer',100000,1,NULL,'2022-04-01');

tests.name: Duplicate names and same hire dates
Zero and negative salaries, boundary dates
Only one department with staff — its headcount equals the average
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin'),(2,'EmptyDept','Nowhere');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Ava','E',100000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'Ben','E',80000,1,1,'2020-01-01');

INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Ava','E',100000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'Ben','E',80000,1,1,'2020-01-01'),(3,'Cara','E',90000,1,1,'2020-01-01'),(4,'Eve','E',70000,2,NULL,'2020-01-01');

Staffed and unstaffed departments — unstaffed ignored in avg
